prompt:
Use case stylized-concept. Create a QUALITY AFFIXES pixel sprite concept sheet matching the approved attached extremely minimal chunky pixel art. Exactly 12 cells, 4 columns x 3 rows, flat charcoal background and readable labels. Same simple diagonal silver-gray sword with brown grip in ALL cells, very coarse 16x16 logical pixel design, nearest-neighbor enlarged, 3-5 colors, big countable square pixels, no detailed textures, no gradients, no smooth glow. Change only a FEW pixels between variants. Heading "QUALITY". Row-major cells:
1 "Neutral": plain clean gray sword baseline.
2 "Broken": tip missing and one large square notch.
3 "Battle Scarred": two small edge notches and one dark blade nick, tip intact.
4 "Worn": duller blade and one frayed grip pixel.
5 "Second Hand": one contrasting replacement grip band and small blade scuff.
6 "Preowned": tiny grip wear only; blade clean.
7 "Like New": bright clean blade, single muted grip pixel.
8 "New": clean neutral blade and fresh even brown grip.
9 "Perfect": uninterrupted bright blade edge and symmetric clean guard.
10 "Masterwork": same blade with simple yellow 3-pixel guard and yellow pommel.
11 "Heirloom": same blade with muted brass guard and two burgundy grip pixels.
12 "Cosmic": same gray blade, one violet pommel pixel and two isolated lavender square spark pixels.
No elaborate objects, no characters, no scene. Preserve the approved minimal pixel-y style; each sword should occupy about 14 logical pixels, blade 2-3 pixels wide. Quality comparisons should be subtle, visible and restrained, not new weapon types. Labels exactly as quoted.

Use case stylized-concept. Make a labeled minimal pixel art affix reference sheet matching the attached approved style. Title "PREFIX VARIATIONS". 6 columns by 4 rows, exactly 24 evenly spaced cells. Every cell contains the SAME basic silver-gray diagonal sword with brown grip, altered as below. Ultra coarse 16x16-style pixel sprites enlarged with large hard square pixels, blade only 2-3 pixels wide, 3-5 flat colors per sprite. Flat charcoal background. No detailed rendering, antialiasing, texture, smooth glows or ornate art. Small simple readable labels beneath each. Changes must be clearly distinguishable but only a few pixels. Keep each sprite simple and generously spaced. Exact row-major order:
Neutral: plain baseline.
Reinforced: thick gray guard band.
Balanced: square gray counterweight pommel.
Precise: single cyan pixel at blade base.
Swift: one pale blue trailing tick near grip.
Featherweight: tiny white 3-pixel feather attached to grip.
Hardened: darker gray blade spine.
Light: slimmer blade and smaller guard.
Heavy: blade one pixel wider.
Short: blade three pixels shorter.
Long: blade two pixels longer.
Blessed: yellow pommel and one tiny gold cross beside tip.
Enchanted: purple guard inset and two violet square sparks.
Charged: three yellow pixels in zigzag beside blade.
Acrobatic: orange loop-shaped small grip tassel.
Ancient: muted bronze guard and one dark rune pixel at blade base.
Keen: bright continuous white edge.
Flaming: three orange/red flame pixels at blade tip.
Poisonous: green blade-edge pixels and one green drip.
Serrated: two square teeth along blade edge.
Refined: clean silver guard and dark blue grip band.
Nimble: two mint ribbon pixels on grip.
Brutal: dark red wrap and squared blade tip.
Sturdy: thick brown grip and gray reinforcing collar.
Labels should be exactly those names, no explanations. Priority is maintaining extreme minimalism of reference. No complex flames, no animals, no characters.

Use case stylized-concept. Create a minimal pixel art STAT SUFFIXES reference sheet matching the attached approved ultra chunky minimal sprites. Flat charcoal background, readable labels. Exactly 5 columns x 3 rows, 15 cells. Every cell same plain diagonal silver sword with brown grip, identical silhouette and palette except a few colored detail pixels. 16x16 logical pixel style enlarged nearest neighbor with large hard square pixels, 3-5 colors per item, no antialiasing, no texture, no glow, no detailed ornament. Title "STAT SUFFIXES". Exact row-major cells and labels:
"Neutral": plain baseline sword.
"Accuracy": one cyan pommel pixel.
"Agility": two mint tassel pixels beside grip.
"Ferocity": two red diagonal wrapping pixels on grip.
"Fleeting": two pale blue horizontal dash pixels trailing tip.
"Intelligence": purple square gem in guard.
"Killing": dark red blade tip, two red pixels.
"Power": orange square pommel, tiny orange blade-base pixel.
"Precision": two cyan aligned notch-like pixels on blade base.
"Protection": compact blue 3-pixel guard cap.
"Rejuvenation": three green pixels forming tiny sprout at pommel.
"Strength": ochre thick grip band.
"Technique": white diagonal 2-pixel grip stitch.
"Vitality": small pink plus at pommel.
"Combined": same sword with cyan pommel Accuracy and red grip Ferocity together, no extra features.
These are proposed visual treatments of stat suffixes. Labels omit 'of' for clarity. Last cell illustrates two coexisting small accents. Extreme simplicity, only a few pixels per detail. No characters or complex symbols.
